question.prompt: The sum of the base-\(10\) logarithms of the divisors of \(10^n\) is \(792.\) What is \(n?\)

solutions.explanation:
Complementary divisors have product \(10^n\), so their logarithms have a particularly simple sum.

Since \(10^n=2^n5^n\), every positive divisor has a unique form \(2^a5^b\), where \(a,b\) are integers from \(0\) through \(n\). Each exponent has \(n+1\) choices, giving \((n+1)^2\) divisors without omissions or repetitions.

Let \(S\) be the sum of their base-\(10\) logarithms. As \(d\) runs through the divisors, \(10^n/d\) runs through the same divisors exactly once. Therefore
\[
2S=\sum_{d\mid 10^n}\left(\log_{10}d+\log_{10}\frac{10^n}{d}\right)
=n(n+1)^2.
\]
This counts every term twice even when a divisor is its own complement, so there is no exceptional square case.

Thus \(n(n+1)^2=1584\). Substituting \(n=11\) gives \(11\cdot12^2=1584\). For nonnegative integers \(n\), the expression \(n(n+1)^2\) strictly increases, so this solution is unique. Hence \(\boxed{n=11}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
solutions.title: Pair complementary divisors

solutions.explanation:
Writing each divisor using its prime exponents lets us add the contributions from \(2\) and \(5\) separately.

Every positive divisor of \(10^n=2^n5^n\) is uniquely \(2^a5^b\), with integers \(0\le a,b\le n\). The independent exponent choices list all \((n+1)^2\) divisors exactly once, and
\[
\log_{10}(2^a5^b)=a\log_{10}2+b\log_{10}5.
\]
Each possible value of \(a\) occurs \(n+1\) times, once for each value of \(b\). The same is true with the exponents reversed. Consequently, the required sum is
\[
(n+1)(0+1+\cdots+n)
\bigl(\log_{10}2+\log_{10}5\bigr).
\]
Using \(0+1+\cdots+n=n(n+1)/2\) and \(\log_{10}2+\log_{10}5=\log_{10}10=1\), this becomes
\[
\frac{n(n+1)^2}{2}=792.
\]
At \(n=11\), the left side is \(11\cdot144/2=792\). It strictly increases as the nonnegative integer \(n\) increases, so no other value works. Thus \(\boxed{n=11}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
